_comment: WHICH LANES TAKE WHICH TURN AT A JUNCTION (ADR-0426; docs/road-model-design.md step 8). The road model states, once,
which turns a junction offers and which arriving lane takes each, from what the road file states: the junction's
arms in order round it (by their stated headings), its `through` pairs (two arms that are one street carrying on),
each arriving lane's kind and slot, and the junction's control. Nothing here is measured: no angle decides a turn.
THE KIND OF A TURN, from arriving arm A into leaving arm B (src/engine/procgen/city/roads/lane_turns.h):
straight   B is A's stated `through` partner;
near_turn  B lies round the junction from A on the kerb side of A's arriving traffic, before A's partner (or, where
A has none, in the half of the other arms nearer A on that side);
far_turn   B lies on the other side (the turn across the oncoming traffic);
(No junction offers a U-turn, B being A itself: a u_turn row is refused when the table is read.)
This world drives on the left: the kerb side comes from one place in the code (lane_graph_build.h kerbPerpSign).
Where A has no partner and B stands exactly halfway round the other arms, the side is not stated: it is taken as
a far turn and reported (the planner should state a through pair or not).
THE ROWS. Each says which arriving lanes take one kind of turn, and into which leaving lanes. EVERY row whose `when`
and `controls` hold at a junction applies there (not only the first): a turn two rows state is kept once. An arriving
lane no row gives a turn is reported, never dropped quietly. Words:
turn      the kind of turn (above);
when      'straight_on': the arriving arm has a way straight on (a stated partner with lanes leaving by it);
'no_straight_on': it has none (the stem of a T); 'any';
controls  the junction's stated control is one of these (absent: any control);
kinds     the arriving lanes' kinds that may take it (the builder's lane kinds: through, turn (a pocket), slip, ramp);
lanes     'every': every arriving lane of those kinds; or {from: 'kerb' | 'centre', count: N}: N lanes counted
from that side; or {from, share: 'more' | 'less'}: where the arm offers both a near and a far turn and
no way straight on, its lanes are shared between them, the kerb side taking the larger half ('more') and
the centre-line side the smaller ('less'); one lane takes both; where only one of the two is offered,
every lane takes it;
into      'same_slot': into the leaving lane of the same slot (counted from the centre line; the nearest there
is where the street beyond has fewer); 'same_side': the k-th lane from the row's side into the k-th
leaving lane from the same side (into the last there is where fewer);
source    where the row comes from: a citation, or [~] a guess to tune.
A turn a row states is a turn the model holds, whether or not it fits its corner: a turn whose drawn corner is too
tight, or would take a vehicle off the paved road, is a CORNER FAULT against that corner (lanes_tool lanegraph lists
them), closed to that vehicle class in the lane-level table until the builder draws the corner to fit (step 9).
LANE LINES (lane_turns.h laneLineBetween: the one rule the lane-level table and the road paint both read). The line
between two neighbouring lanes may be crossed both ways (painted dashed), except: where both lanes are of a kind
listed in `hold_before_stop_line` and both run to the same stop line, the line is solid (painted solid, not to be
crossed) for the road file's `lane_rules.solid_before_stop_line` metres before that stop line.

lane_lines.source: [~] CVC 21460 (a solid line is not crossed) with MUTCD 3B.04 para 30 (solid lane lines on junction approaches discourage lane changing); which kinds hold is a guess: a pocket or slip lane is still being moved into there

turns.source: [~] each lane carries on in its own lane: CVC 21658 (a) (drive within a single lane) read across the junction; the slot rule is a convention
CVC 22100 (a): the turn toward the kerb is made from the lane nearest the kerb, into the lane nearest the kerb (read for driving on the left)
CVC 22100 (b): the turn across the oncoming traffic is made from the lane nearest the centre line, into the lane nearest it (read for driving on the left)

[~] where an arm cannot go straight on, its lanes share the two turns, the kerb side the near turn: CVC 22100 with two turn lanes (MUTCD 3B.20 lane-use arrows for multiple turn lanes); the split is a guess
[~] as the row above, the centre-line side the far turn
